A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of the same OPA-DPO paper. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original OPA-DPO evaluations on LLaVA-1.5-7B and 13B, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, helpfulness evaluations, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same expert revision, LoRA-SFT alignment, and subsequent DPO procedure with language correction, image focus, and anchored preference losses.

E1.justification: Both use the same RLAIF-V training data and evaluate AMBER, MMHalBench, Object HalBench, POPE, and LLaVA-Bench. The appendix image-description and false-premise scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in both the main benchmark comparisons in Table 2 and the helpfulness comparisons in Table 8. No evaluated baseline is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix A.1 retain the same model sizes, sample counts, metrics, greedy evaluation, and training settings, including two OPA epochs followed by four DPO epochs. Ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: The policy-distribution and data-size analyses, OPA and component ablations in Tables 3–4, hyperparameter sweeps in Table 9, and qualitative cases are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same distribution summaries, and Table 1 retains averaging over 200 responses. Neither version introduces or revises seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout, including the appendices. For example, Table 2 retains 7B OPA-DPO's AMBER HalRate of 11.6 and Object Hal CHAIRs of 13.00 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The on-policy definition, KL-divergence Fact 1, gradient analysis, and Equations 1–10 are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about DPO's reliance on on-policy data, OPA-DPO's contributions, and competitive hallucination mitigation using 4.8k training samples.

C2.justification: Both retain the same mechanism explanations and qualifications concerning conservative responses, omitted details, GPT-4V feedback errors, and repetition under certain ablations or hyperparameters. No substantive interpretation or limitation changes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-site link and repeats the repository link in the abstract. The repository link and model/data availability statement already appeared in v1's Appendix A; implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6, the algorithm taxonomy, Table 5, and the 62 cited works retain the same research positioning. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect text reflow.

P1.justification: v2 adds funding acknowledgments and front-page link text, and corrects punctuation around footnote 3 in the appendix overview. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited column and page reflow, including Section 4.1 moving from page 4 to page 5. All 14 figures and nine tables retain their content and design; appendix pages 13–18 render identically.

improvement.justification: The project link, prominent repository pointer, and funding acknowledgments improve discoverability and attribution slightly. However, v1 already documented resource access, and v2 leaves the methods, reasoning, evidence, results, and limitations unchanged, including the appendices. These limited administrative and presentation edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
